title: UAP secrecy justified under a law enforcement provision

tellings.quote: he noticed that they are justifying secrecy under a law enforcement provision rather than just National Security

The DoD organization, AARO, has been labeling many documents with a B7 exemption, which Greenewald says does not make any sense. They are stating that anything AARO does is involved in a law enforcement investigation, which allows AARO to not release it.

plain: The Pentagon's UFO office, known as AARO, is said to be holding back many of its records by claiming they are part of law enforcement investigations, rather than by the usual national security reasons. The journalist Michael Shellenberger told Congress on 13 November 2024 that AARO has been stamping documents with a "B7 exemption", the part of a US law that lets anyone request government records which allows records tied to law enforcement to be withheld. He was repeating a researcher of government records named John Greenewald Jr., who says this "does not make any sense", and he raised it again with Michels the next day. If it is true, the office would be treating everything it does as a police matter so it can keep it secret.
